# Case study: rebuilding and testing mountline.dev

*Generated by `scripts/evidence/build-evidence.mjs` from the raw runs in `docs/case-study/runs`. Edit the scripts, not this file.*

This is the record behind **“And yes, we tested it.”** on the homepage. The subject is Mountline’s own homepage and its inquiry and receptionist-demo paths, measured before and after the September 2026 rebuild. Bramble, the dog groomer on the homepage, is a design example and is not part of this study.

## Builds and environment

- **Before:** commit `52092aa` — the homepage as it was live before the rebuild. Measured from a separate checkout of that commit.
- **After:** `52092aa+tree:0cc460f7f4cf` — the rebuilt homepage, as a local production build.
- **Recorded:** 2026-09-29.
- **Machine:** Apple M5 (10 cores), macOS. **Browser:** Chrome 154.0.8037.58, headless.
- **Tools:** Playwright 1.63.0, axe-core 4.13.0, Lighthouse 13.5.0, Node v26.0.0.
- **Screens:** Desktop 1440 × 900; Phone 390 × 844 (emulated, touch). Phone results are from Chrome’s phone emulation, not a physical phone.
- **Network:** Both builds served locally by `next start`. Lighthouse simulates a slow 4G connection and a 4× slower processor.
- Both builds were production builds (`next build`, then `next start`), with the same `.env.local`.

## Method

1. Before any change, a separate checkout of the live commit was built and served, and `scripts/evidence/site-checks.mjs` was run against it (`runs/baseline.json`), along with the code test suites (`runs/unit-baseline.json`).
2. After the rebuild, the same script ran against the finished build (`runs/final.json`). It finds things the way a visitor does (roles, labels, visible text), so the same checks work on both designs. A few checks only apply to the new page and are marked “—” before.
3. Lighthouse ran 5 times per build per preset, **alternating the two builds** (`runs/lighthouse-compare.json`) so drift over the session affects both equally. Medians are reported with the full range.
4. The homepage shows these results, so the build that was measured showed “not measured yet” in its results panel. The published page differs from the measured build only in `lib/case-study/evidence.json` (and the generated docs). The same checks were run again on the published version (`runs/published-check.json`): 29 of 29 passed.
5. The form check fills the hidden bot-check field on purpose. The server validates the submission and refuses it before saving, so no inquiry, email, or database row is created. Saving itself is covered by the code tests, which run the real database function in an in-process Postgres.

## Customer task checks

| Check | What it shows | Before · desktop | Before · phone | After · desktop | After · phone |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| The offer is on the first screen | The headline and a way to start a project are visible without scrolling. | pass | pass | pass | pass |
| One tap reaches the form | “Talk about your project” lands on the form’s first field. | pass | pass | pass | pass |
| Asking about a service fills it in | “Ask about Capture” opens the form with Photo and video already chosen. | pass | pass | pass | pass |
| The same for the receptionist | “Ask about the receptionist” opens the form with it already chosen. | pass | pass | pass | pass |
| Mistakes are explained | Sending an empty form lists what’s missing and moves to the first problem. | pass | pass | pass | pass |
| Nothing typed is lost | After a mistake, everything already typed is still there. | pass | pass | pass | pass |
| The server checks every message | A controlled test submission reaches the server, is checked, and is refused on purpose, so nothing is saved. | pass | pass | pass | pass |
| The example starts at once | Pressing play on the receptionist example starts it immediately. | pass | pass | pass | pass |
| The outcome is always in reach | The example’s finished message can be read without waiting for the end. | pass | pass | pass | pass |
| The real demo line is next to it | The phone number for the live demo line is shown with the example. | pass | pass | pass | pass |
| Keyboard users can skip ahead | The first key press offers a jump straight to the content. | pass | pass | pass | pass |
| You can always see where you are | Every stop on the keyboard path, down to the form, is visibly highlighted. | pass | pass | pass | pass |
| Automated accessibility scan | axe-core finds no WCAG A/AA rule failures on the page. | **FAIL** | **FAIL** | pass | pass |
| Nothing spills off the side | No sideways scrolling at 360, 390, 768, 1024, 1440, or 1920 pixels wide. | pass | pass | pass | pass |
| The browser demo never fakes a call | With the microphone blocked, or the browser demo switched off, it says so and offers the phone line instead. | — | — | pass | pass |

**After:** 27 of 27 checks passed (desktop and phone counted separately; the accessibility scan is reported below).

### Failures, as recorded

- Before, desktop: **automated-accessibility-scan** — 1 rule(s) failed across 10 element(s): color-contrast×10
- Before, phone: **automated-accessibility-scan** — 1 rule(s) failed across 1 element(s): list×1
- Mid-build (interim-1, 2026-09-29 20:58 UTC, development server), phone: **project-link-reaches-form** — "Your name" field in view after one click. Fixed, then retested in the final run.

## Accessibility scan (axe-core, WCAG 2.2 A and AA)

| Viewport | Rule | Impact | Elements | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Before** | | | | |
| desktop | `color-contrast` | serious | 10 | Elements must meet minimum color contrast ratio thresholds |
| phone | `list` | serious | 1 | <ul> and <ol> must only directly contain <li>, <script> or <template> elements |
| **After** | | | | |

Before: 2 rule(s), 11 element(s). After: 0 rule(s), 0 element(s). An automated scan finds some problems, not all; it is not an accessibility audit.

## Lab performance (Lighthouse)

Median (fastest–slowest) of each build’s runs. Largest contentful paint (LCP) and total blocking time (TBT); fonts, scripts, and total are transfer sizes.

| Build · preset | LCP | TBT | CLS | Fonts | Scripts | Total |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Before · mobile | 6.55 s (6.55 s–6.56 s) | 57 ms (49–60) | 0 | 411 KB | 495 KB | 1024 KB |
| After · mobile | 5.22 s (5.21 s–5.22 s) | 97 ms (92–108) | 0 | 138 KB | 506 KB | 801 KB |
| Before · desktop | 1.24 s (1.23 s–1.28 s) | 0 ms (0–0) | 0 | 411 KB | 495 KB | 1024 KB |
| After · desktop | 1.07 s (1.07 s–1.08 s) | 0 ms (0–0) | 0 | 138 KB | 506 KB | 801 KB |

These are lab numbers from one laptop with Lighthouse’s simulated slow 4G and slower processor. They compare the two builds under the same conditions; they don’t predict any particular visitor’s phone.

## Browser voice demo: failure paths

Run against a separate build with placeholder Retell settings and an unreachable Supabase address, so no call could be created, billed, or saved. Placeholder Retell settings and an unreachable Supabase URL; no real call was possible. Tests 3–6 simulate server or provider answers.

| Case | Result | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `mic-refused` | pass | Talk shown=true; after refusal phase=error; call requests=0 |
| `server-error-shown` | pass | "Something went wrong on our side. Please try again in a moment, or call the demo line."; requests=1; phone offered=true; try again offered=true |
| `rate-limit-shown` | pass | limit message shown; try again offered=false |
| `connect-failure-shown` | pass | phases seen: permission → connecting → error; gateway attempts=1 |
| `double-click-one-request` | pass | requests after a double click=1 |
| `cancel-while-connecting` | pass | phase=rest; Talk back=true; end requests=1; gateway attempts=0 |

Not covered: a real connection, live audio, the post-call transcript and summary from Retell, and microphone behaviour on physical phones.

## Issues found and fixed during the rebuild

- **A link that missed on phones.** A mid-build test caught “Talk about your project” landing on the word-built mark on phones, with the form below the screen. The form now comes right after the heading. Mid-build: **FAIL**; final: pass. Source: The “One tap reaches the form” check, mid-build run and final run.
- **Content that moved while scrolling.** A mid-build test caught content shifting as a desktop screen scrolled past this scene, because the frame resized itself to become a phone. The old homepage had none. Now it changes shape without moving anything. Mid-build: 0.0646 layout shift, desktop; final: 0 layout shift, desktop. Source: Scripted scroll through the whole page with a 4× slower processor, mid-build run and final run.
- **Fonts nobody saw.** The old homepage loaded 411 KB of fonts, including a serif only our team dashboard uses. Now that one loads only there. Before: 411 KB of fonts; final: 138 KB of fonts. Source: Median of the Lighthouse mobile runs.
- **Text too faint to read.** A scan found 10 bits of text too faint to read, mostly faded questions in the old scrolling list. Every line now clears the minimum. Before: 10 faint elements; final: 0 faint elements. Source: axe-core color-contrast rule, desktop and phone. (In the written report and the accessibility tile, not the Refine chapter.)

## Not tested

- Conversations with the live AI receptionist. No test calls were approved for this build, so its answers are not scored here.
- A real browser call to the demo. With placeholder settings, its error paths were exercised (6 of 6 behaved as designed), but no real call was made because the provider keys aren’t set up yet.
- Email delivery to a real inbox. A provider accepting an email doesn’t prove it arrived.
- Physical phones. Phone results come from an emulated phone screen in desktop Chrome.

## Limits

- Lab measurements from one computer on one day. Your customers’ phones and connections will differ.
- Automated accessibility scans catch some problems, not all of them.
- These are recorded results, not a test running in your browser now.

## Reproduce

```bash
# Build and serve each version (a separate checkout for the old commit), then:
node scripts/evidence/site-checks.mjs --base http://localhost:3100 --label baseline --commit <old sha>
node scripts/evidence/site-checks.mjs --base http://localhost:3200 --label final --commit <new sha>
node scripts/evidence/unit-tests.mjs --label baseline --cwd <old checkout>
node scripts/evidence/unit-tests.mjs --label final
node scripts/evidence/compare-lighthouse.mjs --before http://localhost:3100 --after http://localhost:3200 --runs 5
node scripts/evidence/build-evidence.mjs
```
